p0001: MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT Between RadialSpark, LLC and Clear Capital Page 1 of 10

p0002: THIS MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT ("Agreement"), dated as of 09/24/2018 (the "Effective Date"), is between Clear Capital (the "Company") and RadialSpark, LLC (the "Contractor"). WHEREAS, Company desires from time to time to retain Contractor to perform certain management consulting services for Company; and WHEREAS, Contractor desires to perform such management consulting services for Company; NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing premises, and the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, the parties hereto agree as follows:

p0003: 1. PURPOSE OF ENGAGEMENT.

p0004: (a) Company agrees to retain Contractor to perform the consulting services for Company, on a task by task basis (the "Services"), and Contractor agrees to furnish the Services on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement. During the term of this Agreement, Company and Contractor will develop and agree upon statements of work defining the Services and work product to be provided by Contractor, Contractor's compensation, additional terms and conditions, if any, applicable to a particular engagement and such other details as the parties deem appropriate (each a "Statement of Work"). A Statement of Work may provide specifications for deliverables to be provided thereunder (the "Specifications"). Statements of Work that are from time to time agreed upon shall reference this Agreement, and shall be executed by the parties and attached hereto and shall form a part hereof. In all instances of a conflict, between the provisions of this Agreement and the specific provisions set forth in a Statement of Work, the provisions of this Agreement shall control.

p0005: (b) Contractor shall provide sufficient qualified personnel to perform the Services in a professional and workmanlike manner in accordance with industry standards. A Statement of Work may designate certain individuals as "Key Personnel" for an engagement, and the parties subsequently may agree in writing that additional individuals are Key Personnel for such engagement. If there are Key Personnel for an engagement, Contractor shall provide the Services through those personnel and such additional personnel of Contractor as Contractor may from time to time determine to be required for the performance of the Services. Company shall have the right to interview and approve such additional personnel at Company's request. If one or more Key Personnel terminate their employment with Contractor or otherwise become

p0006: unavailable to work on an engagement for reasons beyond Contractor's reasonable control, Contractor may provide the Services through other personnel with comparable training and experience. If Company becomes dissatisfied with any of Contractor's personnel providing the Services, Company may notify Contractor of the details of its dissatisfaction, and the parties shall cooperate to remedy the problem as soon as possible. If Company reasonably requests, Contractor shall reassign the individual who is the subject of Company's dissatisfaction and replace that person with other personnel in accordance with this Agreement.

p0007: (c) Unless otherwise provided in a Statement of Work, Contractor shall provide the Services at Contractor's facility. Contractor shall provide computing equipment consistent with the Services to be provided under the Statement of Work. When services are provided at a Company facility, Company shall provide workspace and other facilities such as computer support consistent with the requirements of the Services to be provided under the Statement of Work. Contractor shall cause its personnel at Company's facility to comply with Company's (i) safety and security rules and other rules applicable to those working in the facility, and (ii) Company's policies concerning access to and security of any Company computer system to which Contractor may have access; provided, that Company has provided Contractor with copies of such rules and policies or has advised Contractor of the existence of such rules and policies.

p0008: (d) Company may request changes that affect the scope or duration of the Services relating to any Statement of Work, including changes in the Specifications and changes in the deliverables to be delivered. Company acknowledges that any change in Specifications may result in changes to estimated fees and estimated timeline for creation of deliverables. Company also may request a change in the Schedule without changing the scope of the Services relating to the applicable Statement of Work. In either case, the parties shall negotiate in good faith a reasonable and equitable adjustment in the applicable fees, Schedule and Specifications. Contractor shall continue work pursuant to the existing Statement of Work, and shall not be bound by any change requested by Company, until such change has been accepted in writing by Contractor.

p0009: (e) The obligations of Company in connection with a particular engagement shall be set forth in the applicable Statement of Work. Company agrees to perform such obligations in accordance with, and subject to, such Statement of Work. Company acknowledges that when a Statement of Work provides that Company's personnel are to work with Contractor's personnel in connection with an engagement, Company's failure to assign Company personnel having skills commensurate with their role with respect to such engagement could adversely affect Contractor's ability to provide the Services.

p0010: (f) To the extent Contractor provides any third party materials and products Contractor acknowledges that it shall be solely responsible for ensuring the functionality and specifications of such third party materials and products used in performing Services under this Agreement.

p0011: 2. TERM. The term of this Agreement shall begin on the date hereof and shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6 hereof.

p0012: 3. CONTRACTOR'S COMPENSATION.

p0013: (a) During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials. In addition, Company shall reimburse Contractor its actual out-of-pocket expenses as reasonably incurred by Contractor in connection with its performance of the Services as negotiated in each Statement of Work.

p0014: (b) Contractor shall bill Company as set forth in the relevant Statement of Work. Each invoice submitted by Contractor will provide supporting detail for the Services invoiced, including, to the extent applicable to a particular engagement, the dates of Services and hours worked at the applicable rate by Statement of Work. Invoices shall also include receipts or other supporting detail concerning related expenses within the billing cycle. Contractor reserves the right to change rates with 30 days notice to Company.

p0015: (c) All fees, charges and other amounts payable to Contractor hereunder do not include any sales, use, excise, value added or other applicable taxes, tariffs or duties, payment of which shall be the sole responsibility of Company (excluding any applicable taxes based on Contractor's net income or taxes arising from the independent contractor relationship between Contractor and its personnel). In the event that such taxes, tariffs or duties are assessed against Contractor, Company shall reimburse Contractor for any such amounts paid by Contractor or provide Contractor with valid tax exemption certificates with respect thereto.

p0016: 4. OWNERSHIP OF MATERIALS RELATED TO SERVICES; ACCEPTANCE.

p0017: (a) The parties agree that all drawings, documents, designs, models, inventions, computer programs, computer systems, data, computer documentation and other tangible materials authored or prepared by Contractor for Company as the work product required by a Statement of Work (collectively, the "Works"), are the property of Company to the extent that such Works were created by Contractor for Company over a time period for which Company has been invoiced and said invoice has been paid. Contractor agrees to render, at Company's sole cost

p0018: and expense, all reasonably required assistance to Company to protect the rights herein above described, including executing other documents as requested by Company.

p0019: (b) Company acknowledges that Contractor provides consulting and development services to other clients, and agrees that nothing in this Agreement shall be deemed or construed to prevent Contractor from delivering on such business. In particular, Company agrees that, notwithstanding anything to the contrary set forth herein:

p0020: (i) as part of Contractor's provision of the Services hereunder, Contractor may utilize its own proprietary works of authorship, that have not been created specifically for Company, including without limitation software, methodologies, tools, specifications, drawings, sketches, models, samples, records and documentation, as well as copyrights, trademarks, servicemarks, ideas, concepts, know-how, techniques, knowledge or data, which have been originated, developed or purchased by Contractor or by third parties under contract to Contractor, and, (ii) Contractor's Information and Contractor's administrative communications and records relating to the Services shall not be deemed to be Works and are and shall remain the sole and exclusive property of Contractor and Company shall not resell or make use of said property in any other manner other than in connection with the software Company receives under this Agreement.

p0021: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.

p0022: (d) Consultant agrees that after Company pays Contractor in full, or after the termination of this agreement, Company may make any changes or additions to the software Consultant created for Company under this Agreement, which Company in Company's discretion may consider necessary, and Company may engage others to make any such changes or additions, without further payments to Consultant.

p0023: 5. CONTRACTOR'S REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES AND WARRANTY DISCLAIMER.

p0024: (a) Contractor represents and warrants to Company that Contractor's performance of the Services called for by this Agreement, to its knowledge, does not and shall not violate any applicable law, rule, or regulation;

p0025: (b) Contractor represents and warrants to Company that Contractor has full authority and sufficient rights, except for rights respecting programs, data and materials provided by Company or identified by Contractor as furnished to Company by third-party vendors, to grant and convey the rights granted to Company under Paragraph 4 hereof;

p0026: (c) Contractor represents and warrants that the Works provided hereunder, including any Contractor Information and any third party products do not infringe any trade secret, trademark, copyright, patent or other proprietary right of any other third party.

p0027: (d) Contractor covenants that it will not offer or pay any bribes (including any offer to provide improper gifts or entertainment) to secure or retain a business advantage (for the benefit of Contractor or for the benefit of Company) at any time during the term of this agreement. Specifically, Contractor agrees that it will not offer or pay any bribes to any person (including, in particular, to any government official) in connection with any aspect of the performance of services under this agreement. Contractor also covenants that at all times during the term of this agreement that it will maintain internal policies and procedures that are reasonably designed to ensure that Contractor's employees and representatives will not offer to pay or pay bribes (or offer or provide improper gifts or entertainment) to any person in connection with Contractor's performance under this agreement.

p0028: Contractor also covenants that it will provide suitable training to its employees and representatives during the term of this agreement about Contractor's anti-corruption policies and procedures. Contractor represents and warrants to Company that Contractor has not offered or paid any bribes (or offered or provided any improper gifts and entertainment) to secure business under this agreement or otherwise in connection with the performance of its obligations under this agreement.

p0029: Notwithstanding any other provision of this agreement, if Contractor offers or pays a bribe or provides improper gifts or entertainment to any government official or to any other person in connection with the performance of Contractor's obligations under this agreement, Company shall be entitled to elect to terminate this agreement effective immediately upon providing to Contractor written notice of such termination, in which case Company shall have no obligation to pay any fees or other consideration to Contractor under this agreement or otherwise.

p0030: (e) THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE IN LIEU OF ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

p0031: 6. TERMINATION.

p0032: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.

p0033: (b) In addition, either party may terminate this Agreement or any outstanding Statement of Work, upon fifteen (15) days written notice to the other party, in the event such other party breaches a material term of this Agreement or any Statement of Work and such breach remains uncured at the end of such fifteen (15) day period. Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination. Contractor shall provide to Company, and hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.

p0034: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

p0035: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.

p0036: (b) NEITHER PARTY SHALL HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY LOST PROFITS OR SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.

p0037: (c) IN ANY SUIT ARISING FROM THIS AGREEMENT EACH PARTY SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ITS OWN ATTORNEYS FEES. COMPANY AND CONTRACTOR HEREBY WAIVE ANY CLAIM TO AWARD OF ATTORNEYS FEES IN SUCH A SUIT.

p0038: 8. CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION. "Confidential Information" means all documents, software, reports, data, records, forms, conversations and other materials obtained by Contractor from Company in the course of performing any Services (including, but not limited to, Company records and information). Notwithstanding the foregoing, Confidential Information does not include information which:

p0039: (i) is or becomes publicly known through no wrongful act of Contractor; or (ii) is independently developed by Contractor without benefit of Company's

p0040: Confidential Information. Contractor shall not use or disclose to any person, firm or entity any Confidential Information without Company's express, prior written permission; provided, however, that notwithstanding the foregoing, Contractor may disclose Confidential Information to the extent that it is required to be disclosed pursuant to a statutory or regulatory provision or court order.

p0041: 9. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR. Contractor is performing the Services as an independent contractor and not as an employee of Company and none of Contractor's personnel shall be entitled to receive any compensation, benefits or other incidents of employment from Company. Subject to Section 3(c), Contractor shall be responsible for all taxes and other expenses arising from the employment or independent contractor relationship between Contractor and its personnel and the rendition of Services hereunder by such personnel to Company. Nothing in this Agreement shall be deemed to constitute a partnership or joint venture between Company and Contractor, nor shall anything in this Agreement be deemed to constitute Contractor or Company the agent of the other. Neither Contractor nor Company shall be or become liable or bound by any representation, act or omission whatsoever of the other.

p0042: 10. NONASSIGNABILITY. Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.

p0043: 11. SEVERABILITY; GOVERNING LAW. In the event that any term or provision of this Agreement shall be held to be invalid, void or unenforceable, then the remainder of this Agreement shall not be affected, impaired or invalidated, and each such term and provision of this Agreement shall be valid and enforceable to the fullest extent permitted by law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.

p0044: (c) In the event of termination under either section 6(a) or 6(b) of this agreement, Contractor shall be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination. Upon receipt of final payment Contractor shall provide to Company, and will assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.

p0045: 12. INTEGRATION. This Agreement, including The Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement and, any Statements of Work entered into pursuant hereto, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties hereto with respect to its subject matter and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous representations, proposals, discussions, and communications, whether oral or in writing. This

p0046: Agreement may be modified only in writing and shall be enforceable in accordance with its terms when signed by each of the parties hereto.

p0047: 13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

p0048: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. At Company's request, Contractor shall provide Company with certificates or other acceptable evidence of insurance or self-insurance evidencing the above coverage and shall provide Company with prompt written notice of any material change.

p0049: 15. Force Majeure. Except for payment obligations hereunder, nonperformance by either party shall be excused to the extent that performance is rendered impossible by strike, acts of God, governmental acts or restrictions, failure of suppliers, or any other reason where failure to perform is beyond the control of the nonperforming party.

p0050: 16. Counterparts. This Agreement may be signed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be an original, with the same effect as if the signatures thereto and hereto were upon the same instrument.

p0051: 17. Entire Agreement. This Agreement constitutes the complete and exclusive agreement between Company and Consultant concerning the work on this project, and it supersedes all other prior agreements, proposals, and representations, whether stated orally or in writing.

p0052: 18. Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the remainder of this Agreement will remain in full force and effect.

p0053: 19. Arbitration. Except as otherwise specified below, all actions, disputes, claims and controversies under common law, statutory law or in equity of any type or nature whatsoever, whether arising before or after the date of this Agreement, and whether directly or indirectly

p0054: relating to:

p0055: (a) this Agreement and/or any amendments and addenda hereto, or the breach, invalidity or termination hereof;

p0056: (b) any previous or subsequent agreement between the parties; and/or (c) any other relationship, transaction or dealing between the parties (collectively the "Disputes"), will be subject to and resolved by binding arbitration pursuant to the Arbitration Rules of U.S. Arbitration & Mediation, (www.usam.com). Any award or order rendered by the arbitrator may be confirmed as a judgment or order in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction, which includes within the federal judicial district of the residence of the party against whom such award or order was entered. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties hereto have caused this Agreement to be executed by their duly authorized representatives as of the Effective Date. /s/ Michael Rockford /s/ John Marcum for RadialSpark, LLC for Clear Capital

# MSA Review — RadialSpark, LLC (Vendor) / Clear Capital (Customer)

**Bottom line:** This is a vendor-drafted agreement with several provisions that are materially off-market against the customer. The highest-priority issues are (1) IP ownership conditioned on payment with no assignment language, (2) a liability cap that is not reciprocal in substance and swallows the IP indemnity, (3) no indemnification obligation running to Company at all (Section 7's heading promises "Indemnification of Contractor," and Section 9 — the carve-out referenced in the cap — is actually the Independent Contractor clause), (4) unilateral rate increases, (5) no data security / privacy obligations despite Clear Capital's business, and (6) an arbitration clause with an obscure provider, no seat, and an attorneys' fee waiver.

---

## Tier 1 — Do Not Sign Without Fixing

### 1. Broken cross-reference guts the liability cap carve-out (¶7(a))
The cap is unlimited "except with respect to Contractor's obligations pursuant to Paragraph 9." Paragraph 9 is **Independent Contractor** — not indemnification (there is no Contractor indemnity anywhere). So the carve-out is meaningless, and Contractor's total liability, including for IP infringement, confidentiality breach, and gross negligence, is capped at fees paid for the specific SOW.

**Fix:** Add a Contractor indemnity (below) and rewrite the carve-out:
> "Notwithstanding the foregoing, the limitations in this Paragraph 7 shall not apply to: (i) Contractor's indemnification obligations under Paragraph [new]; (ii) breach of Paragraph 8 (Confidential Information) or Paragraph [new] (Data Security); (iii) Contractor's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud; (iv) Contractor's breach of Paragraph 5(d) (Anti-Corruption); or (v) death, bodily injury, or damage to tangible property caused by Contractor."

### 2. No indemnity in Company's favor (¶5(c), ¶7)
Contractor *warrants* non-infringement (¶5(c)) but there is no obligation to defend or indemnify. A warranty without an indemnity means Company funds its own defense against a third-party claim and can only recover capped damages.

**Fix:** Insert:
> "Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Company and its affiliates, officers, directors and employees from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting losses, damages, liabilities, settlements, and reasonable attorneys' fees and costs, arising from: (a) any allegation that the Works, Services, Contractor Information, or third-party materials supplied by Contractor infringe or misappropriate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret or other intellectual property right; (b) Contractor's breach of Paragraph 8 or its data security obligations; (c) Contractor's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (d) any claim by Contractor personnel for employment status, wages, taxes, or benefits from Company; and (e) Contractor's breach of Paragraph 5(d). Company shall provide prompt notice and reasonable cooperation; Contractor shall not settle any claim imposing non-monetary obligations on Company without Company's consent."

Also add an IP remedy: at Contractor's expense, procure the right to continue use, or replace/modify to be non-infringing while maintaining conformance to Specifications; refund only as a last resort.

### 3. IP ownership is conditional and there is no present assignment (¶4(a), ¶4(d), ¶6(b)/(c))
Works belong to Company only "to the extent … created … over a time period for which Company has been invoiced and said invoice has been paid." ¶4(a) says Works "are the property of Company" but contains **no assignment, no work-made-for-hire language, and no waiver of moral rights**. ¶4(d) further implies Company cannot modify the software until "paid in full." And ¶6(b) says Contractor assigns work-in-progress, while ¶11(c) — a stray subsection misnumbered under Governing Law — conditions that same assignment on "receipt of final payment." These conflict.

Practical risk: a good-faith invoice dispute leaves Company without title to deliverables it is actively using.

**Fix:**
- Delete the payment condition in ¶4(a) and the "after Company pays Contractor in full" condition in ¶4(d). Contractor's remedy for nonpayment should be a payment claim, not IP forfeiture.
- Add: "Contractor hereby irrevocably assigns to Company all right, title and interest, including all intellectual property rights, in and to the Works, effective upon creation. To the extent any Works constitute works made for hire under 17 U.S.C. § 101, they shall be deemed such. Contractor waives all moral rights in the Works."
- Add a fallback license so Company is never dark: "In the event of any dispute, Company retains an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify, and create derivative works of all Works delivered or in progress."
- Fix the ¶4(a) assistance clause: further-assurances cooperation should be at **Contractor's** cost where reasonably needed to perfect Company's rights, and should include a power of attorney if Contractor fails to execute.
- Reconcile the duplicate/conflicting termination-assignment provisions (¶6(b), ¶11(c)) — keep one, unconditional.

### 4. Contractor Information license is too narrow; ¶4(b)(ii) use restriction (¶4(c), ¶4(b))
The license to embedded Contractor Information omits **distribution and the right to have third parties exercise the rights on Company's behalf**, and is limited to "Company's business operations" — problematic if Clear Capital's deliverable is embedded in a product or service delivered to *its* customers, or if Company divests a business unit. ¶4(b)(ii) also bars Company from making "use of said property in any other manner other than in connection with the software Company receives."

**Fix:**
> "…a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid, non-exclusive license, with the right to sublicense, to use, copy, modify, create derivative works of, distribute, perform and display such Contractor Information, alone or as incorporated in the Works, for any purpose in connection with Company's and its affiliates' business, including permitting contractors, service providers, and successors to exercise these rights on Company's behalf."

Add: "Contractor shall not incorporate into the Works any open source software subject to a copyleft or reciprocal license without Company's prior written consent, and shall disclose all open source components in writing."

### 5. No data security, privacy, or data-return obligations
For a company in the real estate valuation/analytics space, this is the most conspicuous gap. There are no obligations regarding safeguards, breach notification, subprocessors, personnel background checks, use of production data, or return/destruction of Company data. GLBA/FCRA-adjacent data and any consumer PII may be in scope, plus state breach-notification statutes.

**Fix:** Add a Data Security and Privacy section (or Exhibit) covering: administrative, technical and physical safeguards consistent with a recognized framework; processing only as necessary to perform Services; no use of production/live data in development or test environments without written approval and de-identification; prohibition on offshore access without consent; breach notification within 24–48 hours with cooperation and remediation at Contractor's cost; return or certified destruction of Company data on termination or request; audit/assessment rights or annual SOC 2 Type II delivery; and flow-down to subcontractors. Confirm whether a DPA and/or GLBA service-provider addendum is needed.

### 6. SOW conflict order is inverted (¶1(a))
"In all instances of a conflict … the provisions of this Agreement shall control." This prevents Company from negotiating project-specific protections (higher caps, fixed fees, milestones, acceptance criteria, security terms) in a SOW.

**Fix:** "…the MSA shall control, except that a Statement of Work shall control to the extent it expressly identifies the MSA provision being modified and states the parties' intent to supersede it for that Statement of Work."

---

## Tier 2 — Significant Commercial and Operational Risk

### 7. Unilateral rate increases (¶3(b))
"Contractor reserves the right to change rates with 30 days notice." This overrides negotiated SOW pricing at will.

**Fix:** "Rates set forth in a Statement of Work are firm for the duration of that Statement of Work. Contractor may propose rate changes for new Statements of Work upon 90 days' written notice, effective no more frequently than annually and not exceeding [3%] or CPI, whichever is less."

### 8. Time-and-materials with no cap, no estimates, no audit (¶3(a), ¶3(b))
Compensation is T&M with no not-to-exceed amount, no obligation to notify when approaching estimate, and no right to withhold disputed amounts or audit records.

**Fix:** Add: each SOW must state a not-to-exceed amount that Contractor may not exceed without prior written authorization; Contractor to notify Company at 80% of the NTE; expenses reimbursable only if pre-approved in writing and compliant with Company's T&E policy; payment terms Net 45 from receipt of a conforming invoice; invoices submitted more than 90 days after Services rendered are waived; Company may withhold disputed amounts in good faith without breach; Company may audit Contractor's time and expense records for 24 months.

### 9. No acceptance procedure despite the heading (¶4)
Paragraph 4 is titled "…; ACCEPTANCE" but contains no acceptance mechanism, no testing period, and no remedy for deliverables that fail Specifications.

**Fix:** Add: "Company shall have [30] days from delivery to test each deliverable against the Specifications. Company may reject non-conforming deliverables with written notice describing the non-conformity; Contractor shall correct and redeliver within [10] business days at no additional charge. If a deliverable fails acceptance after [two] correction cycles, Company may (i) reject and receive a refund of amounts paid for that deliverable and dependent deliverables, or (ii) accept with an equitable fee reduction. Payment does not constitute acceptance."

### 10. Services warranty is missing / disclaimer is broad (¶1(b), ¶5(e))
The "professional and workmanlike manner" language sits in ¶1 as a covenant, not a warranty with a remedy. ¶5(e) then disclaims all implied warranties. ¶5(a) is qualified "to its knowledge" — legal compliance should be absolute. There is no warranty of conformance to Specifications, no malicious-code warranty, and no warranty period.

**Fix:**
- Delete "to its knowledge" in ¶5(a).
- Add: "Contractor warrants that (i) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel in accordance with applicable industry standards; (ii) for [90] days after acceptance, the Works will conform to the Specifications and operate free of material defects; and (iii) the Works will be free of viruses, malware, back doors, disabling code, or other harmful code. Contractor's remedy obligation is to re-perform or correct at no charge; if it cannot do so within [30] days, Company may terminate the affected Statement of Work and receive a refund of fees paid for the non-conforming Services."
- Preserve non-infringement (¶5(c)) as an unqualified warranty — note it is currently well-drafted in Company's favor; keep it and resist any "to Contractor's knowledge" qualifier.

### 11. Change control lets Contractor veto but Company cannot stop work (¶1(d))
Contractor "shall not be bound by any change requested by Company, until such change has been accepted in writing by Contractor" — with no obligation to respond within any period and no Company right to stop or suspend.

**Fix:** Make it mutual: no change is binding on either party until signed by both; Contractor to respond to change requests with a written impact assessment within 5 business days; add Company's right to suspend Services under an SOW upon written notice, with fees only for Services performed prior to suspension.

### 12. Termination for convenience is illusory (¶6(a))
Termination for any reason is available only "at any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding." Because the MSA continues until terminated and SOWs are the whole point, Company is effectively locked in for the life of every SOW with no exit.

**Fix:** Add: "Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience upon [30] days' written notice, in which case Company shall pay only for Services properly performed and non-cancellable expenses incurred through the termination date." Also add Company termination rights for: Contractor insolvency/bankruptcy/assignment for benefit of creditors; change of control of Contractor; and repeated failure to meet SOW milestones. Add a transition-assistance obligation (up to 60–90 days at then-current rates) with delivery of all Works, source code, documentation, credentials, and Company data.

### 13. Cure period is short and non-differentiated (¶6(b))
Fifteen days is fine for Company but also gives Contractor only 15 days to terminate for a payment dispute. Add: no termination for non-payment of amounts Company disputes in good faith and has notified Contractor of; payment breaches require written notice and a 15-day cure from notice.

### 14. Key Personnel protections are weak (¶1(b))
Contractor may substitute Key Personnel for any reason "beyond Contractor's reasonable control," and may add personnel it "determines to be required" — Company's approval right applies only "at Company's request," which is circular.

**Fix:** Contractor shall not remove or reassign Key Personnel without Company's prior written consent except due to death, disability, or resignation; replacements subject to Company's prior written approval with equal or better qualifications; no charge for ramp-up/knowledge transfer of replacement personnel. Company may require removal of any personnel from the engagement upon notice (not merely "cooperate to remedy"). Add background check and, where applicable, confidentiality-agreement requirements for all personnel with access to Company systems or data.

### 15. Third-party materials (¶1(f)) — good clause, but incomplete
¶1(f) helpfully puts functionality risk on Contractor. Add: Contractor must obtain and pay for all third-party licenses necessary for Company's use of the Works, disclose them in the SOW, and pass through all warranties and indemnities; no third-party terms bind Company without prior written consent.

---

## Tier 3 — Legal / Dispute Mechanics

### 16. Confidentiality is one-way and structurally deficient (¶8)
Only Contractor is bound; only information "obtained by Contractor from Company" is covered — so Contractor's *observations*, derived analyses, and Company information Contractor creates may be outside scope. Missing: standard-of-care obligation, need-to-know limitation, personnel/subcontractor flow-down, notice before compelled disclosure, no-residuals confirmation, return/destruction, survival period, and equitable relief. Note ¶12 references a separate Mutual NDA as part of the Agreement — confirm it exists, obtain a copy, and address any conflict.

**Fix:** Add: standard of care no less than reasonable care and no less than Contractor uses for its own confidential information; disclosure only to personnel with a need to know who are bound by written obligations at least as protective; prompt written notice and cooperation before compelled disclosure so Company may seek a protective order, and disclosure limited to the minimum required; return or destroy on request; obligations survive [5] years, and indefinitely for trade secrets and personal information; Company entitled to injunctive relief without bond. Confirm there is no "residuals" clause anywhere in the Mutual NDA.

### 17. Arbitration clause is problematic (¶19)
- The provider ("U.S. Arbitration & Mediation," identified by a URL) is not a major administrator; its rules are incorporated sight-unseen and may be amended unilaterally.
- No seat/venue, no number of arbitrators, no arbitrator qualifications, no allocation of fees.
- Scope is extraordinarily broad — "any previous or subsequent agreement" and "any other relationship, transaction or dealing between the parties," including disputes "arising before" the Agreement. This could sweep in unrelated matters.
- No carve-out allowing either party to seek injunctive relief in court for IP or confidentiality breaches — a serious gap given the Works and data at issue.
- Combined with ¶7(c)'s mutual attorneys' fee waiver, Company bears its own costs even in a clear-cut win.

**Fix:** Either (a) delete arbitration in favor of exclusive jurisdiction in courts in [Company's home venue] with a jury waiver, or (b) substitute AAA Commercial Rules (or JAMS), single arbitrator with relevant industry/technology experience, seat in [Company's venue], and add: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to protect its intellectual property or Confidential Information." Narrow scope to disputes "arising out of or relating to this Agreement." Delete the ¶7(c) fee waiver or make fees awardable to the prevailing party.

### 18. Governing law and venue (¶11)
Arizona law ("the laws of the Arizona") with no venue designation, paired with an arbitration clause whose confirmation venue is defined by reference to the *residence of the party against whom the award was entered* — i.e., Company can be dragged to Contractor's home forum. Confirm whether Arizona is acceptable; otherwise change to Company's home state.

### 19. Assignment restriction blocks Company reorganizations (¶10)
Company cannot assign even to an affiliate or in a merger, and Contractor's consent standard ("not unreasonably withheld") still requires a negotiation at the worst possible moment.

**Fix:** "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Company may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without consent to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or of the business unit to which this Agreement relates. Contractor may not subcontract any portion of the Services without Company's prior written consent and remains fully responsible for the acts and omissions of any approved subcontractor."

### 20. Force majeure is over-broad (¶15)
"Failure of suppliers" and "any other reason where failure to perform is beyond the control of the nonperforming party" are too generous, and there is no time limit or Company termination right.

**Fix:** Delete "failure of suppliers"; require the affected party to use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate and resume; add: "If a force majeure event continues for more than [30] consecutive days, Company may terminate the affected Statement of Work without liability other than for Services properly performed prior to the event." Confirm force majeure does not excuse Contractor's confidentiality or data security obligations.

### 21. Insurance limits and structure (¶14)
$1M CGL and $1M E&O are low for a technology/data engagement, and there is **no cyber liability / technology E&O coverage** and no requirement that Company be named additional insured or that the policies be primary and non-contributory.

**Fix:** CGL $1M per occurrence / $2M aggregate; Professional Liability/Technology E&O $2–5M including cyber liability, network security, privacy liability, and breach response costs; Workers' Comp per statute plus Employer's Liability $1M; commercial auto if applicable; umbrella as appropriate. Add: insurers rated A- or better; Company named additional insured on CGL; waiver of subrogation; coverage primary and non-contributory; 30 days' notice of cancellation or material change; certificates delivered at signing and annually. Also add: "Maintenance of insurance does not limit Contractor's liability under this Agreement."

### 22. Non-solicitation is mutual — check impact (¶13)
Mutual and reasonably scoped, but note it bars Company from *hiring* Contractor personnel who worked on the Services for one year post-termination. If Company might want to bring key developers in-house, negotiate a carve-out for general solicitations (job postings, recruiters not targeted at the other party) and for individuals who apply unsolicited or who left the other party more than [6] months prior. Also confirm enforceability of any such restriction under applicable law.

### 23. Tax gross-up is broad (¶3(c))
Company bears "other applicable taxes, tariffs or duties." Add: Company is not responsible for taxes based on Contractor's income, gross receipts, property, payroll, or employment; Contractor is responsible for penalties and interest arising from its failure to timely invoice or remit; Contractor shall separately state taxes on invoices and cooperate in claiming exemptions.

### 24. Drafting cleanups
- **Duplicate/conflicting clauses:** ¶11 (Severability; Governing Law) vs. ¶18 (Severability); ¶12 (Integration) vs. ¶17 (Entire Agreement). ¶17 says the Agreement is the "complete and exclusive agreement," which conflicts with ¶12's inclusion of the Mutual NDA and SOWs, and refers to "this project" (singular) and "Consultant." **Delete ¶17 and ¶18**; retain ¶11 and ¶12 as amended.
- **Misnumbered stray subsection:** ¶11(c) (termination payment/assignment) belongs in ¶6 and conflicts with ¶6(b). Resolve.
- **"Consultant" vs. "Contractor":** ¶4(d) and ¶17 use "Consultant," an undefined term. Conform to "Contractor."
- **"a time and materials"** (¶3(a)) is incomplete — should read "on a time and materials basis" and cross-reference the SOW.
- **Missing survival clause.** Add: "Paragraphs 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, and [new indemnity, data security] survive termination or expiration."
- **No notices provision.** Add addresses, permitted methods, and deemed-receipt rules.
- **No records/audit right.** Covered above for fees; consider a general compliance audit right.
- **No compliance/records obligations** for the anti-corruption covenant (¶5(d)) — add an audit right and a representation regarding sanctions/export controls and debarment lists if relevant.
- **No SOW template or minimum contents.** Add a required-elements list (scope, deliverables, Specifications, acceptance criteria, schedule/milestones, Key Personnel, NTE amount, rates, assumptions, dependencies).
- **Signature block** shows Michael Rockford signing "for RadialSpark" and John Marcum "for Clear Capital" — confirm signatory authority and titles, and confirm the correct legal entity name for Clear Capital (e.g., "Clear Capital, LLC" / "Clear Capital.com, Inc.").
- **¶5(d) forfeiture:** the anti-corruption clause states Company "shall have no obligation to pay any fees" upon such termination. This is favorable to Company but may be challenged as a penalty; it is worth keeping, but do not rely on it as the sole remedy.

---

|---|---|---|

| 2 | Contractor indemnity for IP, confidentiality, data breach, GN/WM (new) | Must have |

p0002: THIS MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT ("Agreement"), dated as of 09/24/2018 (the "Effective Date"), is between Clear Capital (the "Company") and RadialSpark, LLC (the "Contractor"). p0029: Notwithstanding any other provision of this agreement, if Contractor offers or pays a bribe or provides improper gifts or entertainment to any government official or to any other person in connection with the performance of Contractor's obligations under this agreement, Company shall be entitled to elect to terminate this agreement effective immediately upon providing to Contractor written notice of such termination, in which case Company shall have no obligation to pay any fees or other consideration to Contractor under this agreement or otherwise.

p0030: (e) THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE IN LIEU OF ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

p0031: 6. TERMINATION.

p0044: (c) In the event of termination under either section 6(a) or 6(b) of this agreement, Contractor shall be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. p0049: 15. Force Majeure. Except for payment obligations hereunder, nonperformance by either party shall be excused to the extent that performance is rendered impossible by strike, acts of God, governmental acts or restrictions, failure of suppliers, or any other reason where failure to perform is beyond the control of the nonperforming party.

p0050: 16. Counterparts. This Agreement may be signed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be an original, with the same effect as if the signatures thereto and hereto were upon the same instrument.

p0051: 17. Entire Agreement. This Agreement constitutes the complete and exclusive agreement between Company and Consultant concerning the work on this project, and it supersedes all other prior agreements, proposals, and representations, whether stated orally or in writing.

p0052: 18. Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the remainder of this Agreement will remain in full force and effect.

p0053: 19. Arbitration. Except as otherwise specified below, all actions, disputes, claims and controversies under common law, statutory law or in equity of any type or nature whatsoever, whether arising before or after the date of this Agreement, and whether directly or indirectly

p0054: relating to:

p0055: (a) this Agreement and/or any amendments and addenda hereto, or the breach, invalidity or termination hereof;

p0056: (b) any previous or subsequent agreement between the parties; and/or (c) any other relationship, transaction or dealing between the parties (collectively the "Disputes"), will be subject to and resolved by binding arbitration pursuant to the Arbitration Rules of U.S. Arbitration & Mediation, (www.usam.com). Any award or order rendered by the arbitrator may be confirmed as a judgment or order in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction, which includes within the federal judicial district of the residence of the party against whom such award or order was entered. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties hereto have caused this Agreement to be executed by their duly authorized representatives as of the Effective Date. /s/ Michael Rockford /s/ John Marcum for RadialSpark, LLC for Clear Capital

# MSA Review — RadialSpark, LLC (Vendor) / Clear Capital (Customer)

**Bottom line:** This is a vendor-drafted agreement with several provisions that are materially off-market against the customer. The highest-priority issues are (1) IP ownership conditioned on payment with no assignment language, (2) a liability cap that is not reciprocal in substance and swallows the IP indemnity, (3) no indemnification obligation running to Company at all (Section 7's heading promises "Indemnification of Contractor," and Section 9 — the carve-out referenced in the cap — is actually the Independent Contractor clause), (4) unilateral rate increases, (5) no data security / privacy obligations despite Clear Capital's business, and (6) an arbitration clause with an obscure provider, no seat, and an attorneys' fee waiver.

---

## Tier 1 — Do Not Sign Without Fixing

### 1. Broken cross-reference guts the liability cap carve-out (¶7(a))
The cap is unlimited "except with respect to Contractor's obligations pursuant to Paragraph 9." Paragraph 9 is **Independent Contractor** — not indemnification (there is no Contractor indemnity anywhere). So the carve-out is meaningless, and Contractor's total liability, including for IP infringement, confidentiality breach, and gross negligence, is capped at fees paid for the specific SOW.

**Fix:** Add a Contractor indemnity (below) and rewrite the carve-out:
> "Notwithstanding the foregoing, the limitations in this Paragraph 7 shall not apply to: (i) Contractor's indemnification obligations under Paragraph [new]; (ii) breach of Paragraph 8 (Confidential Information) or Paragraph [new] (Data Security); (iii) Contractor's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud; (iv) Contractor's breach of Paragraph 5(d) (Anti-Corruption); or (v) death, bodily injury, or damage to tangible property caused by Contractor."

### 2. No indemnity in Company's favor (¶5(c), ¶7)
Contractor *warrants* non-infringement (¶5(c)) but there is no obligation to defend or indemnify. A warranty without an indemnity means Company funds its own defense against a third-party claim and can only recover capped damages.

**Fix:** Insert:
> "Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Company and its affiliates, officers, directors and employees from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting losses, damages, liabilities, settlements, and reasonable attorneys' fees and costs, arising from: (a) any allegation that the Works, Services, Contractor Information, or third-party materials supplied by Contractor infringe or misappropriate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret or other intellectual property right; (b) Contractor's breach of Paragraph 8 or its data security obligations; (c) Contractor's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (d) any claim by Contractor personnel for employment status, wages, taxes, or benefits from Company; and (e) Contractor's breach of Paragraph 5(d). Company shall provide prompt notice and reasonable cooperation; Contractor shall not settle any claim imposing non-monetary obligations on Company without Company's consent."

Also add an IP remedy: at Contractor's expense, procure the right to continue use, or replace/modify to be non-infringing while maintaining conformance to Specifications; refund only as a last resort.

### 3. IP ownership is conditional and there is no present assignment (¶4(a), ¶4(d), ¶6(b)/(c))
Works belong to Company only "to the extent … created … over a time period for which Company has been invoiced and said invoice has been paid." ¶4(a) says Works "are the property of Company" but contains **no assignment, no work-made-for-hire language, and no waiver of moral rights**. ¶4(d) further implies Company cannot modify the software until "paid in full." And ¶6(b) says Contractor assigns work-in-progress, while ¶11(c) — a stray subsection misnumbered under Governing Law — conditions that same assignment on "receipt of final payment." These conflict.

Practical risk: a good-faith invoice dispute leaves Company without title to deliverables it is actively using.

**Fix:**
- Delete the payment condition in ¶4(a) and the "after Company pays Contractor in full" condition in ¶4(d). Contractor's remedy for nonpayment should be a payment claim, not IP forfeiture.
- Add: "Contractor hereby irrevocably assigns to Company all right, title and interest, including all intellectual property rights, in and to the Works, effective upon creation. To the extent any Works constitute works made for hire under 17 U.S.C. § 101, they shall be deemed such. Contractor waives all moral rights in the Works."
- Add a fallback license so Company is never dark: "In the event of any dispute, Company retains an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify, and create derivative works of all Works delivered or in progress."
- Fix the ¶4(a) assistance clause: further-assurances cooperation should be at **Contractor's** cost where reasonably needed to perfect Company's rights, and should include a power of attorney if Contractor fails to execute.
- Reconcile the duplicate/conflicting termination-assignment provisions (¶6(b), ¶11(c)) — keep one, unconditional.

### 4. Contractor Information license is too narrow; ¶4(b)(ii) use restriction (¶4(c), ¶4(b))
The license to embedded Contractor Information omits **distribution and the right to have third parties exercise the rights on Company's behalf**, and is limited to "Company's business operations" — problematic if Clear Capital's deliverable is embedded in a product or service delivered to *its* customers, or if Company divests a business unit. ¶4(b)(ii) also bars Company from making "use of said property in any other manner other than in connection with the software Company receives."

**Fix:**
> "…a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid, non-exclusive license, with the right to sublicense, to use, copy, modify, create derivative works of, distribute, perform and display such Contractor Information, alone or as incorporated in the Works, for any purpose in connection with Company's and its affiliates' business, including permitting contractors, service providers, and successors to exercise these rights on Company's behalf."

Add: "Contractor shall not incorporate into the Works any open source software subject to a copyleft or reciprocal license without Company's prior written consent, and shall disclose all open source components in writing."

### 5. No data security, privacy, or data-return obligations
For a company in the real estate valuation/analytics space, this is the most conspicuous gap. There are no obligations regarding safeguards, breach notification, subprocessors, personnel background checks, use of production data, or return/destruction of Company data. GLBA/FCRA-adjacent data and any consumer PII may be in scope, plus state breach-notification statutes.

**Fix:** Add a Data Security and Privacy section (or Exhibit) covering: administrative, technical and physical safeguards consistent with a recognized framework; processing only as necessary to perform Services; no use of production/live data in development or test environments without written approval and de-identification; prohibition on offshore access without consent; breach notification within 24–48 hours with cooperation and remediation at Contractor's cost; return or certified destruction of Company data on termination or request; audit/assessment rights or annual SOC 2 Type II delivery; and flow-down to subcontractors. Confirm whether a DPA and/or GLBA service-provider addendum is needed.

### 6. SOW conflict order is inverted (¶1(a))
"In all instances of a conflict … the provisions of this Agreement shall control." This prevents Company from negotiating project-specific protections (higher caps, fixed fees, milestones, acceptance criteria, security terms) in a SOW.

**Fix:** "…the MSA shall control, except that a Statement of Work shall control to the extent it expressly identifies the MSA provision being modified and states the parties' intent to supersede it for that Statement of Work."

---

## Tier 2 — Significant Commercial and Operational Risk

### 7. Unilateral rate increases (¶3(b))
"Contractor reserves the right to change rates with 30 days notice." This overrides negotiated SOW pricing at will.

**Fix:** "Rates set forth in a Statement of Work are firm for the duration of that Statement of Work. Contractor may propose rate changes for new Statements of Work upon 90 days' written notice, effective no more frequently than annually and not exceeding [3%] or CPI, whichever is less."

### 8. Time-and-materials with no cap, no estimates, no audit (¶3(a), ¶3(b))
Compensation is T&M with no not-to-exceed amount, no obligation to notify when approaching estimate, and no right to withhold disputed amounts or audit records.

**Fix:** Add: each SOW must state a not-to-exceed amount that Contractor may not exceed without prior written authorization; Contractor to notify Company at 80% of the NTE; expenses reimbursable only if pre-approved in writing and compliant with Company's T&E policy; payment terms Net 45 from receipt of a conforming invoice; invoices submitted more than 90 days after Services rendered are waived; Company may withhold disputed amounts in good faith without breach; Company may audit Contractor's time and expense records for 24 months.

### 9. No acceptance procedure despite the heading (¶4)
Paragraph 4 is titled "…; ACCEPTANCE" but contains no acceptance mechanism, no testing period, and no remedy for deliverables that fail Specifications.

**Fix:** Add: "Company shall have [30] days from delivery to test each deliverable against the Specifications. Company may reject non-conforming deliverables with written notice describing the non-conformity; Contractor shall correct and redeliver within [10] business days at no additional charge. If a deliverable fails acceptance after [two] correction cycles, Company may (i) reject and receive a refund of amounts paid for that deliverable and dependent deliverables, or (ii) accept with an equitable fee reduction. Payment does not constitute acceptance."

### 10. Services warranty is missing / disclaimer is broad (¶1(b), ¶5(e))
The "professional and workmanlike manner" language sits in ¶1 as a covenant, not a warranty with a remedy. ¶5(e) then disclaims all implied warranties. ¶5(a) is qualified "to its knowledge" — legal compliance should be absolute. There is no warranty of conformance to Specifications, no malicious-code warranty, and no warranty period.

**Fix:**
- Delete "to its knowledge" in ¶5(a).
- Add: "Contractor warrants that (i) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel in accordance with applicable industry standards; (ii) for [90] days after acceptance, the Works will conform to the Specifications and operate free of material defects; and (iii) the Works will be free of viruses, malware, back doors, disabling code, or other harmful code. Contractor's remedy obligation is to re-perform or correct at no charge; if it cannot do so within [30] days, Company may terminate the affected Statement of Work and receive a refund of fees paid for the non-conforming Services."
- Preserve non-infringement (¶5(c)) as an unqualified warranty — note it is currently well-drafted in Company's favor; keep it and resist any "to Contractor's knowledge" qualifier.

### 11. Change control lets Contractor veto but Company cannot stop work (¶1(d))
Contractor "shall not be bound by any change requested by Company, until such change has been accepted in writing by Contractor" — with no obligation to respond within any period and no Company right to stop or suspend.

**Fix:** Make it mutual: no change is binding on either party until signed by both; Contractor to respond to change requests with a written impact assessment within 5 business days; add Company's right to suspend Services under an SOW upon written notice, with fees only for Services performed prior to suspension.

### 12. Termination for convenience is illusory (¶6(a))
Termination for any reason is available only "at any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding." Because the MSA continues until terminated and SOWs are the whole point, Company is effectively locked in for the life of every SOW with no exit.

**Fix:** Add: "Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience upon [30] days' written notice, in which case Company shall pay only for Services properly performed and non-cancellable expenses incurred through the termination date." Also add Company termination rights for: Contractor insolvency/bankruptcy/assignment for benefit of creditors; change of control of Contractor; and repeated failure to meet SOW milestones. Add a transition-assistance obligation (up to 60–90 days at then-current rates) with delivery of all Works, source code, documentation, credentials, and Company data.

### 13. Cure period is short and non-differentiated (¶6(b))
Fifteen days is fine for Company but also gives Contractor only 15 days to terminate for a payment dispute. Add: no termination for non-payment of amounts Company disputes in good faith and has notified Contractor of; payment breaches require written notice and a 15-day cure from notice.

### 14. Key Personnel protections are weak (¶1(b))
Contractor may substitute Key Personnel for any reason "beyond Contractor's reasonable control," and may add personnel it "determines to be required" — Company's approval right applies only "at Company's request," which is circular.

**Fix:** Contractor shall not remove or reassign Key Personnel without Company's prior written consent except due to death, disability, or resignation; replacements subject to Company's prior written approval with equal or better qualifications; no charge for ramp-up/knowledge transfer of replacement personnel. Company may require removal of any personnel from the engagement upon notice (not merely "cooperate to remedy"). Add background check and, where applicable, confidentiality-agreement requirements for all personnel with access to Company systems or data.

### 15. Third-party materials (¶1(f)) — good clause, but incomplete
¶1(f) helpfully puts functionality risk on Contractor. Add: Contractor must obtain and pay for all third-party licenses necessary for Company's use of the Works, disclose them in the SOW, and pass through all warranties and indemnities; no third-party terms bind Company without prior written consent.

---

## Tier 3 — Legal / Dispute Mechanics

### 16. Confidentiality is one-way and structurally deficient (¶8)
Only Contractor is bound; only information "obtained by Contractor from Company" is covered — so Contractor's *observations*, derived analyses, and Company information Contractor creates may be outside scope. Missing: standard-of-care obligation, need-to-know limitation, personnel/subcontractor flow-down, notice before compelled disclosure, no-residuals confirmation, return/destruction, survival period, and equitable relief. Note ¶12 references a separate Mutual NDA as part of the Agreement — confirm it exists, obtain a copy, and address any conflict.

**Fix:** Add: standard of care no less than reasonable care and no less than Contractor uses for its own confidential information; disclosure only to personnel with a need to know who are bound by written obligations at least as protective; prompt written notice and cooperation before compelled disclosure so Company may seek a protective order, and disclosure limited to the minimum required; return or destroy on request; obligations survive [5] years, and indefinitely for trade secrets and personal information; Company entitled to injunctive relief without bond. Confirm there is no "residuals" clause anywhere in the Mutual NDA.

### 17. Arbitration clause is problematic (¶19)
- The provider ("U.S. Arbitration & Mediation," identified by a URL) is not a major administrator; its rules are incorporated sight-unseen and may be amended unilaterally.
- No seat/venue, no number of arbitrators, no arbitrator qualifications, no allocation of fees.
- Scope is extraordinarily broad — "any previous or subsequent agreement" and "any other relationship, transaction or dealing between the parties," including disputes "arising before" the Agreement. This could sweep in unrelated matters.
- No carve-out allowing either party to seek injunctive relief in court for IP or confidentiality breaches — a serious gap given the Works and data at issue.
- Combined with ¶7(c)'s mutual attorneys' fee waiver, Company bears its own costs even in a clear-cut win.

**Fix:** Either (a) delete arbitration in favor of exclusive jurisdiction in courts in [Company's home venue] with a jury waiver, or (b) substitute AAA Commercial Rules (or JAMS), single arbitrator with relevant industry/technology experience, seat in [Company's venue], and add: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to protect its intellectual property or Confidential Information." Narrow scope to disputes "arising out of or relating to this Agreement." Delete the ¶7(c) fee waiver or make fees awardable to the prevailing party.

### 18. Governing law and venue (¶11)
Arizona law ("the laws of the Arizona") with no venue designation, paired with an arbitration clause whose confirmation venue is defined by reference to the *residence of the party against whom the award was entered* — i.e., Company can be dragged to Contractor's home forum. Confirm whether Arizona is acceptable; otherwise change to Company's home state.

### 19. Assignment restriction blocks Company reorganizations (¶10)
Company cannot assign even to an affiliate or in a merger, and Contractor's consent standard ("not unreasonably withheld") still requires a negotiation at the worst possible moment.

**Fix:** "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Company may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without consent to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or of the business unit to which this Agreement relates. Contractor may not subcontract any portion of the Services without Company's prior written consent and remains fully responsible for the acts and omissions of any approved subcontractor."

### 20. Force majeure is over-broad (¶15)
"Failure of suppliers" and "any other reason where failure to perform is beyond the control of the nonperforming party" are too generous, and there is no time limit or Company termination right.

**Fix:** Delete "failure of suppliers"; require the affected party to use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate and resume; add: "If a force majeure event continues for more than [30] consecutive days, Company may terminate the affected Statement of Work without liability other than for Services properly performed prior to the event." Confirm force majeure does not excuse Contractor's confidentiality or data security obligations.

### 21. Insurance limits and structure (¶14)
$1M CGL and $1M E&O are low for a technology/data engagement, and there is **no cyber liability / technology E&O coverage** and no requirement that Company be named additional insured or that the policies be primary and non-contributory.

**Fix:** CGL $1M per occurrence / $2M aggregate; Professional Liability/Technology E&O $2–5M including cyber liability, network security, privacy liability, and breach response costs; Workers' Comp per statute plus Employer's Liability $1M; commercial auto if applicable; umbrella as appropriate. Add: insurers rated A- or better; Company named additional insured on CGL; waiver of subrogation; coverage primary and non-contributory; 30 days' notice of cancellation or material change; certificates delivered at signing and annually. Also add: "Maintenance of insurance does not limit Contractor's liability under this Agreement."

### 22. Non-solicitation is mutual — check impact (¶13)
Mutual and reasonably scoped, but note it bars Company from *hiring* Contractor personnel who worked on the Services for one year post-termination. If Company might want to bring key developers in-house, negotiate a carve-out for general solicitations (job postings, recruiters not targeted at the other party) and for individuals who apply unsolicited or who left the other party more than [6] months prior. Also confirm enforceability of any such restriction under applicable law.

### 23. Tax gross-up is broad (¶3(c))
Company bears "other applicable taxes, tariffs or duties." Add: Company is not responsible for taxes based on Contractor's income, gross receipts, property, payroll, or employment; Contractor is responsible for penalties and interest arising from its failure to timely invoice or remit; Contractor shall separately state taxes on invoices and cooperate in claiming exemptions.

### 24. Drafting cleanups
- **Duplicate/conflicting clauses:** ¶11 (Severability; Governing Law) vs. ¶18 (Severability); ¶12 (Integration) vs. ¶17 (Entire Agreement). ¶17 says the Agreement is the "complete and exclusive agreement," which conflicts with ¶12's inclusion of the Mutual NDA and SOWs, and refers to "this project" (singular) and "Consultant." **Delete ¶17 and ¶18**; retain ¶11 and ¶12 as amended.
- **Misnumbered stray subsection:** ¶11(c) (termination payment/assignment) belongs in ¶6 and conflicts with ¶6(b). Resolve.
- **"Consultant" vs. "Contractor":** ¶4(d) and ¶17 use "Consultant," an undefined term. Conform to "Contractor."
- **"a time and materials"** (¶3(a)) is incomplete — should read "on a time and materials basis" and cross-reference the SOW.
- **Missing survival clause.** Add: "Paragraphs 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, and [new indemnity, data security] survive termination or expiration."
- **No notices provision.** Add addresses, permitted methods, and deemed-receipt rules.
- **No records/audit right.** Covered above for fees; consider a general compliance audit right.
- **No compliance/records obligations** for the anti-corruption covenant (¶5(d)) — add an audit right and a representation regarding sanctions/export controls and debarment lists if relevant.
- **No SOW template or minimum contents.** Add a required-elements list (scope, deliverables, Specifications, acceptance criteria, schedule/milestones, Key Personnel, NTE amount, rates, assumptions, dependencies).
- **Signature block** shows Michael Rockford signing "for RadialSpark" and John Marcum "for Clear Capital" — confirm signatory authority and titles, and confirm the correct legal entity name for Clear Capital (e.g., "Clear Capital, LLC" / "Clear Capital.com, Inc.").
- **¶5(d) forfeiture:** the anti-corruption clause states Company "shall have no obligation to pay any fees" upon such termination. This is favorable to Company but may be challenged as a penalty; it is worth keeping, but do not rely on it as the sole remedy.

| 2 | Contractor indemnity for IP, confidentiality, data breach, GN/WM (new) | Must have |
